offering_description.value: Old Republic underwrites specialty commercial property and casualty insurance and surety bonds for businesses and public entities. Its title insurance subsidiaries protect property buyers, owners and mortgage lenders and provide closing and settlement services through independent agents and company offices.

primary_products.value: commercial auto insurance; workers’ compensation insurance; commercial property and liability insurance; surety bonds; title insurance

primary_services.value: title searches and examinations; real estate escrow and settlement; closing services

customer_segment.value: B2B: trucking fleets, contractors, employers, commercial property owners, real estate developers and mortgage lenders; B2C: homebuyers and homeowners purchasing title insurance or closing services; B2G: public entities purchasing specialty property and casualty coverage

end_markets.value: commercial trucking and transportation; construction; commercial and industrial operations; residential real estate and mortgage lending; commercial real estate

revenue_model.value: interest or premiums: premiums on commercial insurance, surety bonds and title policies; service fees: fees for title searches, escrow, settlement and closing

value_chain_position.value: financial intermediary: assumes insured risks and issues policies and bonds to businesses, property owners and lenders; service provider: reviews property records and handles settlement for buyers, sellers and lenders

geography_served.value: North America: United States and Canada, with title operations concentrated in the United States

specialization.value: related lines: specialty commercial property and casualty insurance, surety, title insurance and real estate settlement

distribution_channels.value: agents / brokers: independent commercial insurance brokers, surety agents and title agents; own locations: company-operated title and settlement offices

regulatory_exposure.value: high: insurance underwriting and title insurance are subject to licensing and oversight by U.S. state and Canadian insurance regulators

notes: The current scope of smaller ancillary insurance lines is uncertain.
